extracted.intended_audience: SDS preparers, manufacturers/importers, employers, and regulatory compliance professionals responsible for hazard communication under OSHA's HCS
extracted.subtask_short: SDS content and HCS alignment requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final regulatory decisions describing what information must appear (or be indicated if used/available) in specific SDS sections to align OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard with GHS revisions, plus related procedural/implementation guidance (e.g., electronic labeling, update timing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of physical and chemical properties on SDS
rubrics_metrics.description: SDS preparers are not required to list the physical and chemical properties in any particular order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA retains flexibility so the order of properties on SDSs need not change to align with Rev. 7; downstream users would not need to relearn locations of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Odor threshold reporting (Section 9 odor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain requirement to report odor threshold by requiring it under the existing odor property in Section 9 with a parenthetical stating "includes odor threshold".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA is adding the parenthetical to prevent confusion; the agency is declining to require a statement regarding olfactory fatigue because that recommendation does not align with Rev. 7 and Section 9 is limited to physical/chemical properties. Manufacturers may elect to include an olfactory fatigue statement but it is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaporation rate (Section 9 vapor pressure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaporation rate is to be included via a parenthetical in Section 9(o) (Vapor pressure) stating "includes evaporation rate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Rev. 7 removed 'evaporation rate' as a separate property (UNSCEGHS rationale: effectively covered by vapor pressure), OSHA agrees evaporation rate information may be important in emergencies and clarifies inclusion via parenthetical rather than as a separate listed property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particle characteristics (new Section 9 physical property)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add 'particle characteristics' as a physical property in Section 9; preparers must include particle characteristics (e.g., particle size distribution, median and range, aspect ratio, specific surface area, surface reactivity, density) when that information is available and appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA will not prescribe an exhaustive list because not all metrics are available for all chemicals. The HCS does not require testing, so manufacturers/importers are not expected to perform testing to obtain these metrics; include measurements if available. Particle characteristics apply to nanoparticles including solid nanoparticles present in liquids (e.g., when liquids are aerosolized). Preparers are not expected to attempt to predict downstream attrition changes to particle characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/limits for particle characteristics requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The particle characteristics requirement is limited to cases where a substance's particle characteristics are available and appropriate; OSHA will not require testing to generate these characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If particle characteristics are not known, importers or manufacturers are not expected to perform testing. Many manufacturers already have such information as a commercial attribute; preparers should provide it when it exists but are not required to create it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiling point/footnote linking alternative boiling point methods (Sections 7 and 9; Appendix D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a footnote referenced in Sections 7 and 9 (and Appendix D) explaining that the boiling point for a flammable liquid for storage determination must be determined by 29 CFR 1910.106(a)(5), which allows an alternate method under certain circumstances, and if an alternative method is used and storage classification differs from Section 2, the preparer must note that on the SDS in Sections 7 and 9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The footnote is intended to ensure accuracy/clarity if storage recommendations differ from Section 2 classification due to use of an alternate boiling point method; the footnote will be included in Appendix D (Table D.1) and referenced in Sections 7 and 9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability and reactivity: hazardous reactions including foreseeable emergencies (Section 10(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 10(c) must include information about the possibility of hazardous reactions, and the text includes the clarification that this includes hazardous reactions associated with foreseeable emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA expects preparers to describe conditions in which hazardous reactions could occur (consistent with GHS guidance). The requirement is a general warning not tied directly to the classification process; it need not enumerate every possible use but should inform downstream users about potential hazardous reaction conditions, including emergencies. Suggestions to limit to 'directed uses' were rejected because they would not capture the intended scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toxicological interactive effects (Section 11(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an SDS preparer has information that components of a mixture interact (synergistic or antagonistic effects) resulting in combined effects that deviate from additive predictions, the preparer should state that on the SDS and describe the nature of the interactive effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interactive effects are discussed in Annex 4 guidance; OSHA recognizes testing/studies are often required but will only require disclosure when toxicological data on interactive effects are available without conducting new testing. This disclosure is intended to fill gaps important for worker safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of alternative information/methods used for toxicological data (Section 11(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: When specific chemical data or information is not available, SDS preparers must indicate if alternative information was used (e.g., SAR, QSAR, read-across) and describe what method was used to derive the toxicological information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA intends preparers to note use of tools such as SAR, QSAR, and read-across and to describe how non-specific or analogue data were translated into toxicological information for the untested chemical. This disclosure helps health and safety professionals evaluate the basis for classifications and downstream control/PPE decisions. Preparers need not perform testing to derive such data; the requirement applies when alternative information/methods were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality threshold for alternative-derived toxicological information
rubrics_metrics.description: SDS preparers must include information derived from alternative methods in Section 11 unless they determine that it is of such poor quality that it would not materially aid hazard communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA acknowledges scientific uncertainty and that SAR/analog/read-across methods vary; preparers should exercise professional judgment about data quality. NIOSH cautioned about poorly defined analogs/SARs; OSHA agrees and allows exclusion only when the preparer reasonably determines the information would not materially aid communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport information wording (Section 14(f) nonmandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Change Section 14(f) non-mandatory transport information to read: 'Transport in bulk according to IMO instruments' (instead of 'Transport in bulk (according to Annex II of MARPOL 73/78 and the IBC Code)') to be consistent with GHS Rev. 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSHA received no objections and is finalizing the proposed revision to align with Rev. 7 and IMO phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for updates to the HCS (OSHA policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA will update the HCS only when significant changes to the GHS warrant realignment to improve worker safety rather than adopting a fixed regular schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency reviewed stakeholder input on various periodic schedules (every 2 revisions, every 4 years, etc.) and concluded it is more prudent to update only when substantive changes occur that justify rulemaking, balancing regulatory costs and worker protection benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations and constraints for electronic labeling (QR codes/RFID/etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA will consider permitting electronic labeling (e.g., QR codes, RFID, website links) but has set forth considerations and constraints: electronic labeling should not replace essential label elements required on the container; SDSs/labels must remain accessible in physical form in the workplace as a backup; access, costs, safety, and format standardization issues must be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholder concerns noted by OSHA include worker access to mobile devices, limited network connectivity, prohibition of personal devices in some workplaces, fire/explosion hazards from electronic devices in classified areas, the need for a standard format across platforms, maintenance of persistent links/online data, and optional vs. mandatory use. OSHA and commenters generally support exploring electronic labeling but expect essential information (signal words, hazard statements, pictograms) to remain on printed labels and for safeguards/backups to be provided for emergencies.
